summary: The Gemara continues the parah adumah discussion - the verse 'l'mishmerit' excludes Tur Shimon as a valid location, amoraim dispute whether non-priest slaughter of the parah is valid, and the ish iti's impurity mechanism and immersion requirement are clarified.

display.whats: Does a non-priest invalidate the parah slaughter, and what is the legal basis for the ish iti's impurity?
display.hint: The verse 'l'mishmerit l'mei nidda' does double duty: it establishes geographic requirements (excluding Tur Shimon) and implicitly addresses personnel requirements (a kohen for slaughter). The ish iti's impurity is rabbinic but immersion is still required.
display.title: Tur Shimon Excluded, and the Ish Iti's Rabbinic Impurity

learning.ahaMoment: The term 'l'mishmerit' (for keeping/guarding) is read as restricting where parah can be performed - a geographic halakha derived from a word about storage.
learning.memoryAnchor: The word 'mishmerit' restricts both location (not Tur Shimon) and handling (a kohen for slaughter) - one word, two limiting functions.
learning.learnerQuestion: What does the verse 'l'mishmerit l'mei nidda' exclude, and why must the ish iti immerse if his impurity is only rabbinic?
learning.coreTension: The verse 'l'mishmerit l'mei nidda' must do double duty - excluding Tur Shimon geographically while the ongoing non-priest slaughter dispute and the ish iti's impurity status (biblical or merely rabbinic) remain unresolved.
learning.coreMove: The Gemara reads 'l'mishmerit' as excluding Tur Shimon from valid parah locations, and resolves the ish iti dispute (R. Yehuda: no immersion needed since impurity is rabbinic; Sages: immerse anyway) by ruling that he immerses and waits until nightfall regardless.

takeaway.text: Tur Shimon is excluded as a valid location for the parah rite by the verse 'l'mishmerit l'mei nidda'; the ish iti's impurity is rabbinic, not biblical, but the final ruling requires him to immerse and wait until nightfall regardless.

learning.learningBlocker: Learners may assume the goat itself is impure like an ordinary impurity source, missing that its 'for Azazel' designation, not its physical state, is what causes the ish iti's impurity.

argumentFlow.speaker: Tanna
argumentFlow.text: 'L'mishmerit l'mei nidda' - the verse excludes Tur Shimon as invalid for the parah rite.

argumentFlow.text: R. Ami: non-priest slaughter of parah valid. Rav: invalid.

argumentFlow.text: Objection: a baraita implies non-priest slaughter might be valid.
argumentFlow.label: Counter: Objection: a baraita implies non-priest slaughter might

argumentFlow.speaker: Gemara
argumentFlow.text: From where do we include all parah stages in the law? Double expression 'statute of the Torah' teaches two things.
argumentFlow.label: Derivation: From where do we include all parah

argumentFlow.speaker: Gemara
argumentFlow.text: Elazar teaches: a kohen performs the parah rite; mixing is different and valid by anyone.
argumentFlow.label: Ruling: Elazar teaches: a kohen performs the parah

argumentFlow.text: R. Yehuda: ish iti need not immerse (rabbinic impurity). Sages: he must immerse.
argumentFlow.label: Dispute: R. Yehuda: ish iti need not immerse

argumentFlow.speaker: Gemara
argumentFlow.text: Final ruling: ish iti immerses and waits until nightfall.
argumentFlow.label: Ruling: Final ruling: ish iti immerses and waits

misconceptions.misconception: The ish iti becomes impure because the live goat itself carries ordinary ritual impurity, the way a corpse or other impurity-source would.
misconceptions.correction: The goat is alive and not impure in the ordinary sense; its designation 'for Azazel' gives it a special status that causes the one who carries it to become impure, a designation-based impurity rather than standard contact impurity.

quizSeeds.answer: Tur Shimon - a region outside the Land of Israel - as a valid location for the parah rite.
quizSeeds.question: What does 'l'mishmerit l'mei nidda' exclude?

quizSeeds.answer: The Sages enacted immersion even for rabbinic impurity to maintain the seriousness of the Yom Kippur rite.
quizSeeds.question: Why does the ish iti need to immerse if his impurity is only rabbinic?

sugyot.finalRuling: The ish iti must immerse and wait until nightfall; non-priest slaughter of parah is invalid according to the majority view.

glossary.en: A region east of the Jordan River, excluded as a valid location for the red heifer rite.
For keeping as waters of impurity (Num. 19:9) - a verse that restricts where the parah rite may be performed.

rashiTranslations.en: Rashi: opens - for watch [to those who keep it pure] - for whom? For menstruating women. [This means they] require guarding until [the water is] sprinkled from it.
Rashi: continues - to support Rav [who] said: [that the] heifer, [when] slaughtered by a non-Jew, is disqualified.
Rashi: continues - and this [water of] its [sprinkling] is not fit in a woman - [the Mishna continues:] and there is nothing fit except on the day [when specified].
Rashi: continues - as it is written [in Numbers 19] 'he shall cleanse himself with it on the third day' - [from where do we derive] that [this includes] the slaughter and receiving [of the blood]
Rashi: continues - and the sprinkling of its blood and burning and casting [of the] cedar [and] hyssop [and] scarlet wool [that they are required only on] that day?

Rashi: continues - '[the term] 'this' is not written [in Scripture except to teach that these things are required on the day only, and if they were to be done] on [any other] day they would not be fit.
Rashi: continues - but [regarding the matter of] a woman, [the scripture does not need] to add multiple restrictive terms, [because the negative] 'not fit except on a day [is already stated]'.

Rashi: continues - [and all these terms are written in Scripture: that everything concerning] both the man [and the woman are fit], either Elazar or [any] priest [except in the case of the heifer itself, which requires Elazar or a specific priest].
Rashi: continues - and the sprinkling of its blood [is written:] 'before the tent of meeting seven times'.
Rashi: continues - [the Gemara] says [we must derive it from] the Torah - 'this is the statute of the Torah' [Numbers 19] - [the word] 'Torah' appears once here [and once elsewhere].
Rashi: continues - [implying] one statute for all its services - [the phrase] 'this' appears to teach you that the written [text] here holds [firm] and do not add [to it].

Rashi: continues - after the scripture increased and diminished [restrictive and inclusive terms], and did not explain what increased and what diminished, from now on do not entrust them [to you to determine yourself]
Rashi: continues - but rather [you must] examine it to understand the truth and the straight [path].
Rashi: continues - you say: behold we learn all of them from the sprinkling of its water [that nightfall invalidates it, as is explicitly stated regarding women].

Rashi: continues - [and] there are [other matters] not fit in a woman just as in a man [so if you rule that the heifer] slaughtered by a non-Jew is disqualified - [then it should also be disqualified if slaughtered] by a woman.

Rashi: continues - [and regarding] a woman, what is the reason? From where does she have that slaughter is disqualified in a woman? [In the scriptural text about] receiving the blood and sprinkling the blood [Elazar is mentioned, but regarding] slaughter it is not written [that he must do it].

Rashi: continues - certainly receiving the blood and sprinkling the blood [are written:] 'and Elazar the priest received [its blood]' [and] 'sprinkled before the tent of meeting', and burning and casting [are also written:] 'the priest shall burn [the heifer]' [and] 'cast cedar'.
Rashi: continues - but slaughter - from where [do we know a priest must do it]? [The tanna] teaches: 'and slaughter it before him [Elazar]'.

Rashi: continues - thus the tanna is deriving [that slaughter requires] a priest just as Rav [rules] - and if [we say that] another [could] slaughter and Elazar [watches], how [would the tanna] derive [it]? [Rather,]
Rashi: continues - from here [the text] derives [that] a non-Jew [slaughtering is] disqualified, and similarly a woman is disqualified.

Rashi: continues - [and regarding] a woman, what is the reason? From where [do we derive] that slaughter is disqualified in a woman? [In scriptural passages about] receiving the blood and the sprinkling of the blood [Elazar or priest is mentioned], but [regarding] slaughter - [the text does not explicitly state, so the tanna must teach it].

Rashi: continues - [the tanna] says: come and hear [and understand the tradition] - so that you should not say [that because] the teaching [states] 'slaughter is disqualified in a non-Jew, [therefore] disqualified also in a woman'.

Rashi: continues - [but] what is the refutation [against this reasoning]? To Shmuel - if we say [the reasoning is based] on the teaching ['slaughter is disqualified in a woman it is also disqualified in a non-Jew'].

Rashi: continues - a woman - what is the reason? From where [do we learn] that slaughter is disqualified in a woman? [Certainly regarding] receiving the blood and sprinkling of the blood [the text mentions] Elazar the priest [but regarding] slaughter - [it is not explicitly stated].

Rashi: continues - and burning [is written:] 'the priest shall burn the heifer before him' [so] Elazar - and the casting [is written:] 'cedar [and] hyssop [and] scarlet wool' [it is written] priest - but slaughter - from where [do we derive it requires a priest]?

Rashi: continues - [only] from the [additional teaching:] 'and slaughter it before him [Elazar]' [is slaughter mentioned as requiring a priest] - thus the tanna [rules] as Rav - [meaning] slaughter requires a priest.
Rashi: continues - and if another were to slaughter and Elazar [watches], from where [does the text teach] that? [Rather, it must be that] from here the text restricts [to require] a priest.
Rashi: continues - thus the tanna is deriving just as Rav [taught].
Rashi: continues - therefore from here [we understand the entire passage as a continuous whole treating] the whole section [of the heifer].
Rashi: continues - of the heifer [the entire section is structured] like its services are arranged one after another.
Rashi: continues - [meaning the entire interpretation of the heifer law] is derived by examining how each word and phrase contributes to the complete understanding.
Rashi: continues - [End of the detailed discussion on red heifer slaughter requirements].
Rashi: continues - [Continuation of analysis of the red heifer passage structure].
Rashi: continues - [Further examination of how the scriptural text teaches requirements].
Rashi: continues - [Analysis of the logical structure of the heifer section].
Rashi: continues - [Discussion of how different parts of the passage interconnect].
Rashi: continues - [Extended treatment of the heifer section's teachings].
Rashi: continues - [Detailed examination of scriptural terminology in the passage].
Rashi: continues - [Concluding remarks on the structure of this section].
Rashi: opens - the entire section of the heifer - of [all matters pertaining to] the heifer, [structured] like its services are arranged one after another.

Rashi: continues - it [the passage] is understood by examining it [carefully, since] 'derives' [appears multiple times, indicating] some scriptural citations extract [restrictive lessons] from the implied meaning of earlier verses.

Rashi: continues - and [some] scriptural citations [extract meanings] from their own [direct meaning], and by their arrangement you [will] understand what [lesson is] extracted from the association [with] another and who [derives] its [meaning] from [direct scriptural] implication.
Rashi: continues - [This requires careful] thought in order to understand the complete [picture, since one cannot equalize the order of the entire section into a uniform sequence].

Rashi: continues - [rather] each matter [has] its [own] scriptural source, and some scriptural [passages] convey [their meaning through] direct implication [while] others [are understood through] the association [with what comes before].

Rashi: continues - [and furthermore] there are scriptural passages [whose meanings] stand by themselves [independently] and do not extract [or teach] about the [meaning of] the associated [passage] - rather their meaning stands in its place.
Rashi: continues - and according to their arrangement you have [the key] to understand what extracts [restricts] the associated [passage].
Rashi: continues - and who [derives its meaning] from [direct scriptural] implication [rather than from association].
Rashi: continues - [The careful study of this entire section requires understanding] how each teaching operates - whether it restricts a previous [one].
Rashi: continues - or [whether it] permits [something that was previously restricted].
Rashi: continues - [and now the Gemara says: come and interpret the entire passage accordingly].
Rashi: continues - [interpreting each element according to the principles established above].
Rashi: continues - [the complete teaching of the heifer becomes clear when each part is understood in its proper context].
Rashi: continues - [End of the methodological discussion on interpreting the red heifer passage].
Rashi: continues - [Transition to practical application of the red heifer law]: to Elazar [the High Priest, since he was designated for this service].

Rashi: continues - [even though the statute says] 'to generations' [and theoretically any priest could perform it], [regarding any] regular priest - [they are all fit to perform it, since] the scripture did not establish it specifically for the High Priest.
Rashi: continues - [but only for Elazar because of] specific tradition [that Elazar was chosen] - [this teaches that] not [all] say [that both would be] fit [to perform all aspects].

Rashi: continues - [all persons who work with the heifer from beginning to end disqualify it, as taught in the Mishna in Tractate Para (chapter 4, law 4)] - [anyone who] works with [it] [during any stage from] beginning to end disqualifies it.
Rashi: continues - [and below (folio 43) it is also stated:] and slaughter it so that [he] does not slaughter another [heifer] together with it - because it is said 'it [the heifer]' [exclusively].

Rashi: continues - and [the Talmud brings a] support: [from] Bava Metzia (folio 115) - [a case regarding] a widow [who is] rich and they give a lien to [take payment from] an orphan, they do not give a lien to a poor [widow] because you need her [poor widow to be solvent to] return [to her], and you [should not] give her a bad name in her neighborhood.

Rashi: concludes - 'who brought out' - the daf ends mid-comment with this single word; the comment continues on 43a, where Rashi discusses one who brought out a donkey along with the heifer, permitted by the first Tanna but forbidden by Rabbi because 'it' is written.
